newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain copied Argentine "dirty war" files - paper.
newsitem.headline: Spain copied Argentine "dirty war" files - paper.

text.p: Spain's spy agency photographed secret documents listing people who had been kidnapped, tortured and killed during Argentina's "dirty war", Spanish daily El Mundo reported on Thursday.
Quoting an Argentine official, El Mundo said the documents had been flown from Buenos Aires to Madrid in eight trunks in 1983 at the end of Argentina's brutal military dictatorship.
The Spanish military intelligence agency CESID microfilmed the records before they were transported in trucks to a bank in Switzerland and placed in a safe deposit where they remain, the paper said.
The files reportedly list thousands of suspected leftists who were abducted and murdered during a campaign of terror orchestrated by the Argentine military dictatorship from 1976-1983.
The documents include the names of hundreds of Spaniards who went missing during the "dirty war" which is the subject of an investigation being conducted by a Spanish judge.

After the democratic election of president Raul Alfonsin in 1983, the newspaper said the military leaders were forced to leave the country and plotted to take the papers to a leading bank in the Swiss city of Lugano.
"Two Hercules jets took off from Argentina, each with a set of the papers to safeguard against an accident or sabotage," the Argentine official was quoted as saying.

Spanish judge Baltasar Garzon, who is investigating the disappearance of about 300 Spaniards during the "dirty war", sent a commision to investigate the safe deposits and accounts of Argentine military leaders in 1996.
Last month, Garzon issued an international arrest warrant for former Argentine military president Leopoldo Galtieri for his alleged role in the killing of three Spaniards.
